newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian shares slip, OMV gains before results.
newsitem.headline: Austrian shares slip, OMV gains before results.

text.p: Austrian shares closed moderately lower on Monday, weighed down by languid Eurobourses as focus honed in on Germany's record Telekom issue, traders said.
The market is seen hemmed in between 1,080 and 1,100 points in the short-term, they added.
The ATX index of 21 blue chips lost 3.10 points, or 0.3 percent, to 1,084.45 with 14 shares falling and seven gaining.
"Not much was going on throughout Europe -- Telekom dominated everything," said one trader.
Overall, trading was quiet with activity centring on OMV, Flughafen, VA Stahl and the two Creditanstalt shares.

Oil and chemicals group OMV was the most actively traded ahead of its nine-month results on Tuesday. OMV, Austria's largest industrial group, gained one schilling to 1,085.0 on turnover of 85,084 lots.
Analysts expect EBIT (earnings before interest and tax) of around 1.96 billion to 2.11 billion schillings in the first nine months. In the year-ago period, EBIT reached 2.03 billion schillings.
Also reporting nine-month results tomorrow is steelmaker Boehler-Uddeholm, which analysts expect will be in line with market expectations. Boehler added on three schillings to 760.
The day's leading decliner was Wolford, shedding 3.5 percent to 1,350 schillings, while Leykam was the top gainer, adding on 1.25 percent to 284.5.
The Vienna Bourse index lost 5.1 points to close at 1,086.9.
The December ATX future fell 5.1 points to 1,086.9 on turnover of 942 lots.
